chips.label: TR-808
chips.prompt: booming Roland TR-808 drum machine: deep tuned kick, snappy snare, crisp closed hats, handclaps and cowbell
chips.desc: Roland's 1980 analog drum machine flopped on release, then became the sound of electro, Miami bass, hip-hop and trap. With its decay turned up, the kick doubles as a sub bass.

chips.label: TR-909
chips.prompt: punchy Roland TR-909 drum machine: driving four-on-the-floor kick, sizzling offbeat open hats, bright clap and crashing ride
chips.desc: Roland's 1983 hybrid machine: analog kick, snare and clap with sampled hats and cymbals. Chicago and Detroit producers made it the backbone of house and techno.

chips.label: TR-707
chips.prompt: crisp Roland TR-707 sampled drums: tight digital kick, clean snappy snare, bright cowbell and tambourine in a mid-80s dance groove
chips.desc: Roland's 1985 all-sample drum machine, clean and slightly thin. A staple of freestyle, Italo disco, early Chicago house and 80s synth-pop.

chips.label: TR-606
chips.prompt: thin, ticking Roland TR-606 analog drums: clicky kick, papery snare and fizzy hi-hats in busy sixteenth-note patterns
chips.desc: Roland's 1981 Drumatix, built as a partner for the TB-303 bass. Its small, clicky analog sounds suit acid, electro, IDM and lo-fi indie.

chips.label: TR-505
chips.prompt: lo-fi Roland TR-505 drum machine: small, boxy sampled kick and snare, plinky congas, timbales and cowbell in a cheerful mid-80s pattern
chips.desc: Roland's 1986 budget PCM drum machine, with tiny lo-fi samples of kick, snare, congas, timbales and cowbells. Cheap and charming, it turns up in early house, bedroom pop and lo-fi electronica.

chips.label: CR-78
chips.prompt: vintage Roland CR-78 rhythm box: soft thumping kick, ticking metallic hi-hat, tambourine and guiro in a gentle preset groove
chips.desc: Roland's 1978 CompuRhythm, among the first drum machines with a microprocessor, so users could store their own patterns. Its soft, ticking, slightly toy-like sound colours late-70s new wave and synth-pop.

chips.label: Vintage rhythm box
chips.prompt: early-70s preset rhythm box: thin, ticking organ-top drum patterns looping a hypnotic, mechanical soul pulse
chips.desc: Boxes like the Ace Tone Rhythm Ace (1967) and Maestro Rhythm King were built to accompany home organists. Their thin, looping presets gave early-70s soul and later bedroom pop a hypnotic, mechanical pulse.

chips.label: LinnDrum
chips.prompt: punchy LinnDrum sampled drums: tight tuned kick, crisp snare with big reverb, claps and cabasa in a polished 80s pop groove
chips.desc: The 1980 Linn LM-1 was the first drum machine to play digital samples of real drums; the cheaper LinnDrum followed in 1982. Tunable, crisp and clean, it is all over 80s pop, R&B and rock.

chips.label: Oberheim DMX
chips.prompt: hard-hitting Oberheim DMX drums: thick boxy kick, cracking sampled snare and stiff hi-hats in an early-80s electro beat
chips.desc: Oberheim's 1981 sampled drum machine hit harder than most rivals. Its blunt kick and loud crack powered early hip-hop, electro and synth-pop.

chips.label: E-mu SP-1200
chips.prompt: gritty E-mu SP-1200 drums: crunchy 12-bit sampled kick and snare, filtered dusty breaks and heavy swing
chips.desc: E-mu's 1987 sampling drum machine: 12-bit, 26 kHz and only ten seconds of sample time. That grainy crunch defined late-80s and 90s golden-era hip-hop.

chips.label: Akai MPC crunch
chips.prompt: punchy Akai MPC drums: crunchy sampled kick and snare finger-drummed on pads with loose, lazy MPC swing
chips.desc: Akai's MPC60 (1988) and MPC3000 (1994) put sampling and sequencing behind 16 rubber pads. Their punch and signature swing shaped hip-hop and neo-soul drums that sit just behind the beat.

chips.label: E-mu Drumulator
chips.prompt: chunky early-80s E-mu Drumulator drums: punchy, slightly dull sampled kick and snare, clicky rimshot and claps in a straight electro-pop beat
chips.desc: E-mu's 1983 Drumulator brought sampled drums in under $1,000. Its short, punchy samples were everywhere in mid-80s pop, rock demos and early hip-hop.

chips.label: Simmons SDS-V
chips.prompt: zappy Simmons SDS-V electronic drums: pitch-sweeping synth toms and a hard electronic snare in big 80s fills
chips.desc: A 1981 British analog electronic kit played on hexagonal pads. Its laser-like descending toms became the signature fill of 80s new wave and pop rock.

chips.label: Alesis HR-16
chips.prompt: late-80s Alesis HR-16 drums: bright, roomy sampled acoustic kit with crisp snare and realistic toms in a stiff, programmed groove
chips.desc: Alesis's 1987 budget drum machine, packed with bright 16-bit acoustic-style samples. A staple of late-80s demos, industrial, early techno and bedroom productions.

chips.label: Elektron-style machine
chips.prompt: modern Elektron-style drum machine: punchy analog kick, crunchy sample hits and parameter-locked hats that change tone every step
chips.desc: Swedish maker Elektron's boxes (Machinedrum 2001, Analog Rytm 2014, Digitakt 2017) let every step lock its own pitch, decay or filter. The result is evolving, glitchy, jam-friendly drums loved in techno and experimental electronica.

chips.label: Tight studio kit
chips.prompt: tight, dry acoustic studio drum kit: punchy close-miked kick, crisp snare and controlled hi-hats with a steady pocket
chips.desc: A well-tuned kit recorded in a dead room with close mics. Clean and punchy, it is the default for pop, singer-songwriter, R&B and polished rock.

chips.label: Big roomy rock kit
chips.prompt: big, roomy rock drum kit: booming kick, huge cracking snare and crashing cymbals captured with loud room mics
chips.desc: Distant room mics and heavy compression make a kit sound enormous. The thunderous sound of 70s arena rock and stadium anthems, played hard on a heavy backbeat.

chips.label: Jazz brushes kit
chips.prompt: small jazz drum kit played with wire brushes: swishing snare sweeps, feathered kick and a soft ride cymbal pattern
chips.desc: Small drums and thin cymbals, with wire brushes stirring circles on the snare head. Intimate and swinging: ballads, piano trios and late-night lounge jazz.

chips.label: 60s soul kit
chips.prompt: vintage 1960s soul drum kit: thuddy deadened kick, woody snare doubled by tambourine on the backbeat, warm and slightly distant
chips.desc: Deadened heads, few mics and analog tape: the warm, thuddy kit of 60s Detroit and Memphis soul records, often doubled by a tambourine on 2 and 4.

chips.label: Amen break
chips.prompt: sped-up, chopped Amen break: rolling, syncopated vintage funk drum break with washy ride and rushing snare edits
chips.desc: A four-bar drum solo from a 1969 funk record, perhaps the most sampled break ever. Sped up and re-chopped, it is the backbone of jungle and drum and bass.

chips.label: Think break
chips.prompt: sped-up Think break: driving funk kick and snare with chopped 'woo, yeah' vocal shouts, high-energy rave and hip-house feel
chips.desc: A 1972 funk drum break famous for its shouted 'woo! yeah!'. Late-80s hip-hop, hip-house and rave producers looped it endlessly, usually sped up.

chips.label: Classic funk break
chips.prompt: looped 1970 funk drum break: syncopated kick, ghost-noted snare and busy sixteenth-note hi-hats, sampled and dusty
chips.desc: Modeled on a 1970 funk drum break that is one of the most sampled ever: syncopated kick, whispering snare ghost notes and steady 16th hats. Looped, it powered late-80s and 90s hip-hop.

chips.label: Chopped breakbeats
chips.prompt: chopped and rearranged breakbeats: sliced vintage drum hits re-sequenced into stuttering, syncopated rolls and edits
chips.desc: Producers slice a sampled drum break into single hits and replay them in a new order. The technique behind jungle, breakbeat, big beat and much boom bap.

chips.label: Funk ghost-note kit
chips.prompt: live funk drum kit: tight kick, crisp backbeat and quiet ghost notes on the snare bubbling between every hit
chips.desc: Ghost notes are barely-there snare taps between the main backbeats. They give live funk, neo-soul and fusion drumming its bubbling sixteenth-note pocket.

chips.label: Trashy garage kit
chips.prompt: loose, trashy garage-rock drum kit: washy cymbals, flappy snare and pounding floor tom played hard and fast
chips.desc: A cheap kit, one or two mics and lots of cymbal wash. Raw and energetic, it is the sound of 60s garage, punk and lo-fi indie rock.

chips.label: Trap hi-hat rolls
chips.prompt: rapid trap hi-hat rolls switching between sixteenths, triplets and thirty-second-note stutters with pitched flams
chips.desc: Machine-gun hi-hats that jump between note values and bend up and down in pitch. The rhythmic signature of Atlanta trap and its offshoots, drill included.

chips.label: Snare roll build
chips.prompt: accelerating 808 snare roll build-up, doubling in speed and rising in pitch into the drop
chips.desc: Snare hits doubling from 8ths to 16ths to 32nds, often pitched upward. The classic tension build before an EDM, trap or dance-pop drop.

chips.label: Rimshot
chips.prompt: dry, woody cross-stick rimshot clicks marking the backbeat with a soft, intimate feel
chips.desc: Hitting rim and head together (rimshot) or laying the stick across the rim (cross-stick) gives a woody click. Used in quiet verses, bossa nova, reggae and ballads; the 808 rim is a dancehall staple.

chips.label: Handclap stack
chips.prompt: layered stack of handclaps on the backbeat, wide and slightly loose like a room full of people clapping
chips.desc: Several claps, real or drum-machine, stacked and spread in stereo for a big human snap. A backbone of disco, house, trap and pop choruses.

chips.label: Finger snaps
chips.prompt: crisp, dry finger snaps on 2 and 4, close and intimate, carrying the backbeat
chips.desc: A minimal backbeat that feels cool and personal. Heard in doo-wop, jazz vocals, minimal pop and R&B, where the snap replaces or doubles the snare.

chips.label: Gated 80s snare
chips.prompt: huge gated-reverb 80s snare: a cannon-like crack with a burst of room sound that cuts off abruptly
chips.desc: Discovered in a London studio around 1979: a noise gate chops off the room reverb on a loud snare. That explosive, clipped crack defined 80s pop and power ballads.

chips.label: Layered trap snare
chips.prompt: layered trap snare and clap hitting hard on beat three, sharp and bright with a short reverb tail
chips.desc: Trap snares are usually a snare and clap stacked, landing on beat 3 because the groove is felt in half-time. Crisp, bright and loud in the mix.

chips.label: Offbeat open hats
chips.prompt: sizzling open hi-hats on every offbeat between four-on-the-floor kicks, driving and bright
chips.desc: The open hat on the 'and' of every beat gives disco, house and garage their pumping lift. With a kick on every beat it makes the classic 'boom-tss'.

chips.label: Ride cymbal pings
chips.prompt: clear, pinging ride cymbal with a bright bell-like stick attack driving a swinging pattern
chips.desc: The ride's 'ding, ding-da-ding' carries the swing in jazz and lifts choruses in rock. Hitting the bell gives a brighter, cutting ping.

chips.label: Crash swells
chips.prompt: rolling mallet cymbal swells rising into big crash hits at every section change
chips.desc: A cymbal rolled with soft mallets swells from a whisper to a roar. Film scores, rock intros and EDM transitions use it to announce a new section.

chips.label: Reversed cymbal
chips.prompt: reversed cymbal swooshes sucking upward into the downbeat of each new section
chips.desc: A cymbal recording played backwards swells up and stops dead. A transition trick in psychedelic rock since the late 60s and everywhere in pop and EDM today.

chips.label: Big tom fills
chips.prompt: rolling tom fills tumbling around the kit into each chorus, big, resonant and powerful
chips.desc: Fills around the toms close one phrase and launch the next section. Big, resonant tom runs are a staple of rock, gospel and power ballads.

chips.label: Congas
chips.prompt: warm, open-toned congas played by hand in an interlocking tumbao pattern with crisp slaps
chips.desc: Tall Afro-Cuban barrel drums played in pairs or threes. The tumbao rhythm of open tones and slaps drives salsa, Latin jazz, disco and house percussion.

chips.label: Bongos
chips.prompt: bright, high-pitched bongos in a steady martillo pattern with crisp slaps and quick rolls
chips.desc: Two small joined drums held between the knees. The martillo ('hammer') pattern is a fixture of Cuban son, salsa and 70s soul and funk.

chips.label: Timbales
chips.prompt: metallic timbales with sharp rimshots, cascara shell patterns and rolling fills into cowbell hits
chips.desc: Shallow metal-shelled drums played with sticks, usually with mounted cowbells. Their cascara shell rhythm and fiery fills lead the band in salsa, mambo and Latin jazz.

chips.label: Shaker
chips.prompt: steady sixteenth-note shaker, soft and airy, adding gentle forward motion to the groove
chips.desc: A seed- or bead-filled shaker played in constant 16ths. The easiest way to add subtle motion to pop, acoustic, house and Afrobeats grooves.

chips.label: Tambourine
chips.prompt: jingling tambourine struck on the backbeat and shaken in sixteenths for bright, driving energy
chips.desc: A frame with metal jingles, hit on 2 and 4 or shaken in 16ths. The sparkle on top of 60s soul, gospel, folk rock and Britpop.

chips.label: Cowbell
chips.prompt: dry, clanky cowbell playing a steady, syncopated pattern that cuts through the mix
chips.desc: A metal bell struck with a stick. It anchors salsa and Latin grooves, and the 808 cowbell is a hallmark of Miami bass, Memphis rap and phonk.

chips.label: Claves
chips.prompt: two hardwood claves clicking out a crisp, bright son clave rhythm
chips.desc: Two hardwood sticks struck together to play clave, the 3-2 or 2-3 rhythmic key that organises Cuban son, salsa and much Latin music.

chips.label: Guiro
chips.prompt: scraped wooden guiro playing a scratchy, rhythmic long-short pattern
chips.desc: A notched gourd scraped with a stick. Its raspy long-short strokes add texture to salsa, cumbia, merengue and bossa nova.

chips.label: Cajon
chips.prompt: deep, slappy cajon played by hand: bass-heavy center thumps and snappy edge slaps
chips.desc: A Peruvian wooden box drum the player sits on. The centre gives a kick-like thump and the edge a snare-like crack, ideal for flamenco and unplugged acoustic sets.

chips.label: Djembe
chips.prompt: resonant djembe hand drum: deep bass tones, ringing open tones and sharp, cracking slaps
chips.desc: A goblet-shaped drum of the Mande peoples of West Africa (Mali, Guinea), played with bare hands. Three core strokes, bass, tone and slap, build its powerful polyrhythms.

chips.label: Taiko
chips.prompt: thunderous Japanese taiko ensemble: massive booming drums struck with thick sticks in powerful unison patterns
chips.desc: Japanese barrel drums, the biggest (odaiko) taller than a person. Ensemble taiko took off in the 1950s and now powers epic trailers, film scores and game music.

chips.label: Frame drum
chips.prompt: deep frame drum played by hand: soft thumps, buzzing snare strings and a hypnotic rolling pattern
chips.desc: Wide, shallow drums like the tar and bendir are among the oldest drums known. Played with the fingers, they give North African, Middle Eastern and meditative music an earthy pulse; the bendir adds a buzzing snare string.

chips.label: Marching snare
chips.prompt: tight, high-tension marching snare drumline with crisp rudiments, rolls and military cadences
chips.desc: Marching snares are cranked tight for a cutting crack. Drumline rudiments and cadences drive military music, HBCU marching bands and stadium anthems.

chips.label: Glitchy foley
chips.prompt: glitchy foley percussion: clicks, crunches, taps and found-sound hits chopped into tight micro-rhythms
chips.desc: Everyday sounds such as keys, paper, pops and mouth clicks used as drums and cut into tiny stuttering fragments. Heard in glitch, IDM, hyperpop and minimal pop.

chips.label: Agogo bells
chips.prompt: bright two-tone agogo bells ringing a high-low syncopated pattern over the groove
chips.desc: A double bell with roots in Yoruba tradition, central to Brazilian samba and Afro-Brazilian music. Its high-low clang ties the whole percussion section together.

chips.label: Samba batucada
chips.prompt: booming Brazilian samba batucada: deep surdo drums, rattling snares, snapping tamborims and whistles in a carnival groove
chips.desc: Batucada is the street-percussion style of Rio's samba schools: surdos pound the bass, caixas and repiques chatter, and tamborims snap. Pure carnival energy.

chips.label: Wind chimes
chips.prompt: shimmering mark tree wind chimes: a glittering cascade of tiny metal bars sweeping up and down
chips.desc: A row of hanging metal bars brushed with a finger or stick. That cascading sparkle signals magic, dreams and transitions in pop, R&B and film.

chips.label: Castanets
chips.prompt: rapid clicking castanets rattling crisp trills and accents in a fiery Spanish rhythm
chips.desc: Pairs of shell-shaped hardwood clappers held in the hands. Their rattling trills are essential to Spanish dance and flamenco-flavoured classical music.

chips.label: 808 sub bass
chips.prompt: deep 808 sub bass: long, booming tuned kick-bass notes rumbling beneath the beat
chips.desc: The TR-808 kick with its decay turned right up, tuned to the song's key and played as a bassline. Usually a sample played chromatically today; the low end of trap, drill and modern hip-hop.

chips.label: Sliding 808 glides
chips.prompt: sliding 808 bass with portamento glides bending between notes, lightly distorted for growl
chips.desc: Glide, or portamento, bends each 808 note into the next. Pitch slides are the defining move of UK drill basslines and a big part of modern trap.

chips.label: Reese bass
chips.prompt: dark Reese bass: two detuned sawtooth waves phasing against each other in a growling, swirling low drone
chips.desc: Named after the alias on a 1988 Detroit techno record, it is two slightly detuned saws beating against each other. Jungle and drum and bass made its menacing rumble a signature.

chips.label: TB-303 acid
chips.prompt: squelchy Roland TB-303 acid bassline: resonant filter sweeps, accents and slides in hypnotic sixteenth-note patterns
chips.desc: Roland's 1981 TB-303 Bass Line was sold as a practice partner for guitarists and flopped. Chicago producers cranked its resonance and accent in the mid-80s and acid house was born.

chips.label: Minimoog bass
chips.prompt: fat Minimoog bass: warm, round analog low end with a punchy filter envelope in a funky, syncopated line
chips.desc: Moog's 1970 Minimoog Model D packed three oscillators and the famous ladder filter into a portable keyboard. Its thick bass fuelled 70s funk, disco, fusion and 90s West Coast G-funk.

chips.label: Juno synth bass
chips.prompt: warm analog synth bass from a Juno-style polysynth: round square-wave notes with a soft filter pluck
chips.desc: Roland's Juno-60 and Juno-106 and similar analog synths make smooth, rubbery bass. Common in synth-pop, synthwave, deep house and Japanese city pop.

chips.label: FM / DX bass
chips.prompt: punchy Yamaha DX7 FM bass: metallic, percussive slap-like attack with a bright, elastic tone
chips.desc: FM synthesis (Yamaha DX7, 1983) gives bass a hard, clanky attack. Its slap-bass presets bounce through mid-80s pop, R&B, new jack swing and city pop.

chips.label: Wobble bass
chips.prompt: wobble bass: thick, growling synth bass with a filter LFO wobbling in time with the beat
chips.desc: An LFO sweeps a low-pass filter so the bass pulses 'wub-wub' in rhythm. Born in mid-2000s UK dubstep and supersized in brostep and riddim.

chips.label: Neuro bass
chips.prompt: aggressive neuro bass: distorted, metallic, constantly morphing mid-range synth bass with sharp rhythmic edits
chips.desc: Neurofunk, a late-90s drum and bass offshoot, is built on layered, heavily processed basses that snarl and mutate every bar. Dark, technical and precise.

chips.label: Sub drop
chips.prompt: deep sub drop: a falling sine-bass boom plunging in pitch right on the downbeat of the drop
chips.desc: A low sine or 808 note that sweeps downward in pitch as an impact at a drop or section change. Felt more than heard in EDM, trap and trailers.

chips.label: Taurus bass pedals
chips.prompt: huge Moog Taurus pedal bass: deep, sustained analog synth bass notes swelling under the band
chips.desc: Moog's 1976 Taurus is a set of foot pedals that plays enormous analog bass. Prog and arena rock bands used it so the bassist's hands were free for guitar or keys.

chips.label: Slap bass
chips.prompt: funky slap bass: thumb-slapped low notes and popped high strings in a percussive, syncopated groove
chips.desc: Thumping the low strings with the thumb and snapping the high ones with a finger, a technique popularised in late-60s funk. Bright and percussive: the voice of funk, disco and 80s pop.

chips.label: Fingerstyle bass
chips.prompt: warm fingerstyle electric bass: round, steady notes locking tightly with the kick drum
chips.desc: Plucking with two fingers gives a warm, rounded tone. The everyday bass of soul, R&B, pop, reggae and gospel; a Precision Bass with flatwound strings is the vintage soul sound.

chips.label: Picked rock bass
chips.prompt: driving pick-played rock bass: bright attack, steady eighth notes and a growly, slightly overdriven tone
chips.desc: A pick gives a sharper attack and a metallic clank. The driving eighth-note bass of punk, classic rock, post-punk and indie.

chips.label: Fretless bass
chips.prompt: singing fretless bass: smooth glides, a vocal 'mwah' tone and melodic slides between notes
chips.desc: With a smooth fingerboard, notes slide freely and bloom with a vocal 'mwah'. Fusion, 80s art pop and smooth jazz used it as a lead voice.

chips.label: Upright bass
chips.prompt: warm upright double bass: plucked walking lines with woody thump and natural resonance
chips.desc: The acoustic double bass played pizzicato with the fingers. Its walking quarter-note lines are the heartbeat of jazz, and slapped it drives rockabilly and bluegrass.

chips.label: Keyboard bass
chips.prompt: soft Rhodes-style keyboard bass: round, thumpy electric piano bass notes played with the left hand
chips.desc: Fender's 1960s Rhodes Piano Bass, a 32-key bass-range electric piano, let keyboardists cover the bass. Its soft, thumpy tone grounds psychedelic rock, soul jazz and lounge combos.

chips.label: Tuba bass line
chips.prompt: bouncing sousaphone bass line: round, brassy low notes pumping on the downbeats
chips.desc: In early jazz and street bands, the tuba or sousaphone played the bass. It still powers New Orleans brass bands, polka, Mexican banda and Balkan brass.

chips.label: Octave disco bass
chips.prompt: octave-pumping disco bass: bouncing eighth notes leaping between low and high octaves
chips.desc: The bass jumps between a note and its octave on every eighth, locking with a four-on-the-floor kick. The engine of 70s disco, Italo and nu-disco.

chips.label: Dub bass
chips.prompt: deep, heavy dub bass: round, slow, melodic sub-heavy lines with lots of space between notes
chips.desc: Reggae and dub push the bass to the front: very low, rounded and melodic, played softly so it is felt in the chest. Jungle, dubstep and UK sound-system music inherited it.

chips.label: Fuzz bass
chips.prompt: fuzzy overdriven electric bass: gritty, saturated growl driving a heavy riff
chips.desc: Running bass through a fuzz pedal or cranked amp adds a buzzing, gritty top. Used in 60s psych, stoner rock, garage and big modern pop-rock choruses.

chips.label: Minimoog lead
chips.prompt: soaring Minimoog lead: fat, singing monophonic tone with pitch-bend wails and mod-wheel vibrato
chips.desc: Played with its pitch and mod wheels, the Minimoog Model D (1970) sounds almost vocal. It defined 70s prog rock, jazz fusion and funk synth solos.

chips.label: Prophet-5 chords
chips.prompt: warm Sequential Prophet-5 polysynth chords: rich, slightly detuned analog voices with a gentle filter sweep
chips.desc: Sequential Circuits' 1978 Prophet-5 was the first fully programmable polyphonic synth that could store its sounds. Its lush, slightly unstable chords fill late-70s and 80s pop and film scores.

chips.label: Prophet synth brass
chips.prompt: punchy Prophet-5 synth brass: bright sawtooth chord stabs with a fast, snappy filter swell
chips.desc: Analog 'synth brass' uses sawtooth waves and a quick filter envelope to mimic a horn section. The Prophet-5 version is a signature of 80s pop and new wave hooks.

chips.label: Juno pad
chips.prompt: lush Juno-106 pad: warm sawtooth chords washed in thick, wobbly stereo chorus
chips.desc: Roland's Juno-60 (1982) and Juno-106 (1984) are affordable analog polysynths with one oscillator per voice. The built-in chorus makes them wide and dreamy: house, synthwave, lo-fi and chillwave.

chips.label: Jupiter-8
chips.prompt: big Roland Jupiter-8 polysynth: wide, glossy analog pads and bright, punchy layered chords
chips.desc: Roland's 1981 flagship, eight voices with two oscillators each. Its rich, polished sound is a staple of 80s synth-pop, Italo disco and modern synthwave.

chips.label: DX7 e-piano
chips.prompt: glassy Yamaha DX7 FM electric piano: bell-like tine attack, chiming and bright, in soft 80s ballad chords
chips.desc: The 1983 DX7 was the first hit digital synth and one of the best-selling ever. Its crystalline FM electric piano preset sits on countless 80s ballads and R&B slow jams.

chips.label: DX7 FM bells
chips.prompt: shimmering Yamaha DX7 FM bells: metallic, glassy tones with a long ringing decay
chips.desc: FM is great at bells: modulating one sine wave with another at odd ratios creates clangorous overtones. The DX7's bell and marimba presets sparkle through 80s pop and new age.

chips.label: CS-80 brass
chips.prompt: swelling Yamaha CS-80 brass: expressive, bittersweet analog chords with ribbon pitch bends, cinematic and vast
chips.desc: Yamaha's famously heavy 1977 CS-80 had a ribbon controller and per-note aftertouch for expressive swells. Its bittersweet brass became the sound of sci-fi film scores.

chips.label: OB-Xa brass stabs
chips.prompt: huge Oberheim OB-Xa brass stabs: fat, detuned analog chords punching out a bold, anthemic riff
chips.desc: Oberheim's early-80s OB-Xa was a big, bold polysynth with up to eight voices. Its brassy, stadium-sized stabs drove 80s rock anthems and synth-pop.

chips.label: Korg M1 house
chips.prompt: bright Korg M1 house piano and organ: punchy digital piano chords and deep organ-bass stabs in classic 90s house
chips.desc: Korg's 1988 M1 workstation sold around 250,000 units. Its bright house piano and organ presets are the sound of early-90s house, garage and Eurodance.

chips.label: PPG Wave
chips.prompt: glassy PPG Wave wavetable synth: metallic digital tones sweeping through shimmering harmonic textures
chips.desc: Germany's PPG Wave (1981) pioneered wavetable synthesis, stepping through stored waveforms for a crisp, grainy, digital-meets-analog shimmer. A favourite of 80s new wave and synth-pop.

chips.label: ARP Odyssey
chips.prompt: biting ARP Odyssey lead: nasal, aggressive analog tone with a screaming filter and squelchy sync
chips.desc: ARP's 1972 Odyssey was a compact duophonic rival to the Minimoog with a sharper, more aggressive filter. Funk, fusion and disco players loved its piercing leads.

chips.label: Mellotron choir
chips.prompt: haunting Mellotron tape choir: wobbly 'aah' vocal chords with tape flutter and a soft attack
chips.desc: The 1960s Mellotron plays real tape recordings, one strip per key, each lasting about eight seconds. Its eerie choir and strings define 60s psychedelia and 70s prog.

chips.label: SH-101
chips.prompt: bubbly Roland SH-101 mono synth: rubbery, squelchy bass-lead lines and sequenced blips
chips.desc: Roland's 1982 SH-101 was a simple, affordable monosynth with a built-in sequencer and arpeggiator. Bargain-priced secondhand by the 90s, it became a rave, acid and electro workhorse.

chips.label: Korg MS-20
chips.prompt: gritty Korg MS-20: raw, snarling leads and basses through an aggressive, screaming resonant filter
chips.desc: Korg's 1978 semi-modular MS-20 has a famously harsh, self-oscillating filter. Industrial, EBM, electroclash and synth-punk love its abrasive scream.

chips.label: Roland D-50
chips.prompt: breathy Roland D-50 digital pad: airy sampled-attack textures with shimmering chorus and reverb, dreamy and late-80s
chips.desc: Roland's 1987 D-50 joined short sampled attacks to synthesized sustains, which it called LA synthesis. Built-in reverb and chorus presets like 'Fantasia' defined late-80s pop and new age pads.

chips.label: Theremin
chips.prompt: eerie theremin: wavering, ghostly sine-like melody gliding between notes with wide, wobbling vibrato
chips.desc: Invented in 1920 and played in the air: one hand near an antenna sets pitch, the other sets volume. Its ghostly wail is the classic sound of 50s sci-fi and horror films.

chips.label: Supersaw
chips.prompt: huge supersaw lead: stacked detuned sawtooth waves, bright, wide and euphoric
chips.desc: Roland's JP-8000 (1996) introduced the 'super saw', seven detuned saws in one voice. Its massive shimmer became the anthem of trance, EDM festival drops and future bass.

chips.label: Synth pluck
chips.prompt: bright synth pluck: short, snappy notes with a quick filter decay bouncing in a melodic pattern
chips.desc: A patch whose filter snaps shut so each note blips like a plucked string. Everywhere in tropical house, progressive house, future bass and pop drops.

chips.label: Warm analog pad
chips.prompt: warm analog pad: soft, slow-attack sawtooth chords under a gentle low-pass filter, swelling underneath
chips.desc: Slow attack, long release and a mellow filter turn a synth into a cushion of sound. Pads glue chords together in ambient, synthwave, R&B and film music.

chips.label: Glassy bell pad
chips.prompt: glassy bell pad: shimmering crystalline attack melting into a soft, airy sustain
chips.desc: Layering a bell-like FM or digital attack over a soft pad gives sparkle and warmth at once. A signature of late-80s digital synths, new age, ambient and lo-fi.

chips.label: String machine
chips.prompt: vintage string machine: thin, buzzy ensemble strings swirling in chorus, warm and slightly synthetic
chips.desc: Divide-down string ensembles like the 1974 ARP Solina used a chorus-like ensemble circuit to fake a section. Their silky, buzzy wash colours 70s disco, prog and synth-pop.

chips.label: Arpeggiator
chips.prompt: bubbling synth arpeggiator: fast sixteenth-note analog arpeggios cycling hypnotically through the chord
chips.desc: An arpeggiator plays a held chord one note at a time in a set pattern and rate. It is the sequenced pulse of 70s Berlin-school electronic music, Italo disco and synthwave.

chips.label: Acid lead
chips.prompt: screaming acid lead: resonant, squelching 303-style line pushed through distortion, rising in intensity
chips.desc: Play the TB-303 an octave up through distortion and it becomes a squealing lead. A peak-time sound in acid techno, acid trance and rave revivals.

chips.label: Portamento lead
chips.prompt: gliding portamento lead: smooth, singing mono synth notes sliding into each other, expressive and vocal
chips.desc: Portamento, or glide, makes a mono synth slide between notes like a voice or slide guitar. Classic for prog and fusion solos and modern trap and drill melodies.

chips.label: Hoover
chips.prompt: rave hoover synth: menacing, detuned, pitch-diving chords with a vacuum-cleaner whine
chips.desc: Born from a Roland Alpha Juno preset around 1990-91, the hoover dives in pitch with a growling, detuned buzz. Iconic in hardcore rave, gabber, jungle and techno.

chips.label: Chiptune square wave
chips.prompt: bleepy 8-bit chiptune square waves: pulse-wave melodies and fast arpeggios like a retro game console
chips.desc: Chiptune uses or imitates the sound chips of 80s consoles and home computers, with only a few pulse, triangle and noise channels. Fast arpeggios fake chords; huge in game music and nostalgic pop.

chips.label: Vocoder chords
chips.prompt: robotic vocoder chords: synth pads shaped by a voice into talking, harmonised robot vocals
chips.desc: A vocoder imprints the shape of a voice onto a synth carrier so chords seem to speak. Its robotic harmony is a staple of electro, disco, funk and French house.

chips.label: Talk box
chips.prompt: funky talk box lead: a synth melody shaped through a mouth tube into smooth, singing, robotic vowels
chips.desc: A talk box pipes a synth or guitar into the player's mouth through a tube, so their mouth shapes the sound. The smooth, vowel-shaped lead of 80s funk and West Coast G-funk.

chips.label: Granular shimmer
chips.prompt: granular shimmer: tiny slices of sound frozen into a glittering, slowly evolving cloud of tones
chips.desc: Granular synthesis chops audio into tiny grains and re-scatters them. The result is a hovering, glistening texture used in ambient, film scores and experimental electronica.

chips.label: Modular bleeps
chips.prompt: modular synth bleeps: random sample-and-hold blips and burbling patch-cable tones, playful and alien
chips.desc: Modular synths, from 60s Moog systems to today's Eurorack, are wired with patch cables. Random voltages make the burbling, computer-like bleeps of IDM, experimental techno and sci-fi scores.

chips.label: Sidechained stabs
chips.prompt: sidechained synth chord stabs: punchy, short house chords ducking and pumping against the kick
chips.desc: Short offbeat chords compressed so they duck every time the kick hits. The pumping feel of French house, deep house and UK garage.

chips.label: Detuned lo-fi keys
chips.prompt: detuned lo-fi synth keys: warbly chords with wobbling tape-flutter pitch drift and a dusty, muffled tone
chips.desc: Slight detune and pitch wobble (wow and flutter) mimic a worn cassette. The hazy, nostalgic keys of lo-fi hip-hop, chillwave and bedroom pop.

chips.label: Wavetable growl
chips.prompt: aggressive wavetable growl: snarling, vowel-like mid bass morphing through distorted, metallic shapes
chips.desc: Modern wavetable synths sweep through waveforms while filters and distortion carve talking 'yoi' and growl sounds. The core of dubstep, riddim and bass music.

chips.label: Sine-wave lead
chips.prompt: pure sine-wave lead: soft, whistling, flute-like synth melody gliding high above a deep, round sub
chips.desc: A sine wave has no overtones, so it sounds pure and whistly. Used for G-funk whistle melodies, minimal techno blips and gentle lullaby-like leads.

chips.label: Noise riser
chips.prompt: white-noise sweep riser: filtered noise swelling up in pitch and volume into a big drop
chips.desc: Filtered white noise with a rising cutoff builds tension before a drop or chorus; reversed, it becomes a downlifter. Essential to EDM, trance, trap and trailer music.

chips.label: Orchestra hit
chips.prompt: dramatic orchestra hit stabs: a sampled full-orchestra blast, punchy and retro, slamming the accents
chips.desc: Sampled from a classical recording into the Fairlight CMI sampler around 1980, the orchestra hit became a hallmark of 80s electro, freestyle, early hip-hop and new jack swing.

chips.label: Trance gate
chips.prompt: trance-gated pad: sustained synth chords chopped into pulsing, rhythmic sixteenth-note stutters
chips.desc: A volume gate chops a held pad into rhythmic 16ths. A staple of 90s and 2000s trance, progressive house and euphoric EDM breakdowns.

chips.label: Hard-sync lead
chips.prompt: tearing hard-sync synth lead: bright, aggressive tone with a ripping, sweeping harmonic edge
chips.desc: Hard sync locks one oscillator to another; sweeping the second one's pitch gives a ripping, vocal sweep. A classic lead in 80s new wave, synth rock and modern electro.

chips.label: Future bass chords
chips.prompt: wobbling future bass chords: detuned supersaw stacks with pitch-bent swells, sidechain pumping and chopped vocal blips
chips.desc: Mid-2010s future bass took fat supersaw chords and made them wobble, bend and pump hard against a half-time beat. Bright, emotional and festival-ready.

chips.label: Ambient drone
chips.prompt: evolving ambient drone: slow, sustained synth tones drifting and shimmering over long stretches of time
chips.desc: Long, slowly changing tones with little rhythm. The foundation of ambient, drone, meditation music and tense film underscore.

chips.label: Grand piano
chips.prompt: bright concert grand piano: full, ringing chords and clear melodic runs with natural hall resonance
chips.desc: The modern grand, with 88 keys and a cast-iron frame, has a vast range of dynamics and colour. Bright and full for pop ballads, jazz, classical and film; nine-foot concert grands have the deepest bass.

chips.label: Upright piano
chips.prompt: warm upright piano: intimate, slightly woody tone, close-miked with soft hammer and pedal noise
chips.desc: Vertical strings make uprights compact and a little boxier than grands. Their homely, close sound suits singer-songwriter, indie, lo-fi and parlour songs.

chips.label: Felt piano
chips.prompt: soft felt piano: muted, hushed notes from felt-dampened hammers with intimate key and pedal noise
chips.desc: A strip of felt between hammers and strings, like an upright's practice pedal, makes notes soft, dark and breathy. The signature of modern neo-classical, ambient and sad-piano music.

chips.label: Honky-tonk piano
chips.prompt: jangly honky-tonk piano: bright, slightly detuned saloon upright pounding out ragtime and boogie rhythms
chips.desc: A piano whose two or three strings per note drift slightly apart, giving a chorus-like jangle. It evokes saloons, ragtime, boogie-woogie and early rock and roll.

chips.label: Rhodes
chips.prompt: warm Fender Rhodes electric piano: bell-like tines, mellow bark when played hard, gentle stereo tremolo
chips.desc: Struck metal tines and pickups give the Rhodes its round, bell-like tone that growls when played hard. Since the 60s it has been the sound of jazz fusion, soul, neo-soul and lo-fi hip-hop.

chips.label: Wurlitzer
chips.prompt: reedy Wurlitzer electric piano: warm, slightly gritty tone that barks and breaks up when played hard
chips.desc: Wurlitzer electric pianos, made from 1954 (the 1970s 200A is the classic), strike steel reeds for a buzzier, more nasal tone than a Rhodes. Heard in 60s soul, 70s soft rock and indie.

chips.label: CP-70 electric grand
chips.prompt: chiming Yamaha CP-70 electric grand: bright, slightly metallic piano with a punchy pickup tone
chips.desc: Yamaha's 1976 CP-70 is a real stringed grand with pickups, built to fold down for touring. Its chiming, jangly tone shines in 80s pop, new wave and synth-pop ballads.

chips.label: Clavinet
chips.prompt: funky Hohner Clavinet: percussive, twangy, wah-filtered keyboard riffs in tight sixteenth-note funk patterns
chips.desc: Hohner's Clavinet (the D6 arrived in 1971) strikes strings with rubber tips for a biting, guitar-like snap. The funk keyboard of the 70s, often through wah or phaser.

chips.label: Hammond B3
chips.prompt: whirling Hammond B3 organ through a Leslie rotary speaker: gospel-style swells, drawbar chords and percussive stabs
chips.desc: Hammond's B3 (1954-1974) builds its tone from spinning tonewheels and drawbars; through a Leslie rotating speaker it swirls and growls. Central to gospel, soul, blues, jazz organ trios and classic rock.

chips.label: Church pipe organ
chips.prompt: majestic church pipe organ: towering full-stop chords, deep pedal bass and vast cathedral reverb
chips.desc: Pipe organs blow air through ranks of pipes chosen by stops, some 32 feet long for floor-shaking bass. Sacred and grand in Baroque music, hymns, gothic horror and epic scores.

chips.label: Reed organ
chips.prompt: wheezy reed organ: breathy pump-organ chords with a soft, accordion-like sustain, homely and rustic
chips.desc: Pump organs and harmoniums push air across free metal reeds, like an accordion. Their wheezy warmth suits folk, old hymns and Indian devotional music, where the hand-pumped harmonium backs singers.

chips.label: 60s combo organ
chips.prompt: buzzy 60s combo organ: thin, bright, reedy Farfisa-style riffs with fast vibrato
chips.desc: Portable transistor organs like the Farfisa and Vox Continental arrived in the early 60s. Their cheesy, cutting buzz is the sound of garage rock, ska and psychedelic pop.

chips.label: Harpsichord
chips.prompt: crisp harpsichord: plucked, bright metallic notes in ornate baroque runs and arpeggios
chips.desc: Quills pluck the strings instead of hammers striking them, so every note jangles at the same volume. The keyboard of the Baroque era, revived in 60s baroque pop and period scores.

chips.label: Celesta
chips.prompt: delicate celesta: tinkling, sweet bell-like keyboard notes, magical and twinkling
chips.desc: Patented in Paris in 1886, its hammers strike metal bars over wooden resonators. Its fairy-dust sound is the classic marker of magic, winter and childhood in ballet and film.

chips.label: Music box
chips.prompt: music box melody: tiny plinking metal-comb notes, fragile and nostalgic, gently slowing down
chips.desc: A pinned cylinder plucks the teeth of a tuned steel comb. Its fragile tinkle signals childhood, nostalgia or creepiness in film, lullabies and lo-fi.

chips.label: Toy piano
chips.prompt: plinky toy piano: small, metallic, slightly out-of-tune notes, playful and quirky
chips.desc: Toy pianos strike metal rods instead of strings, so they plink like a glockenspiel. Used for whimsical, quirky or eerie touches in indie pop, film and contemporary classical.

chips.label: Mellotron flutes
chips.prompt: dreamy Mellotron flutes: wobbly, breathy tape-replay flute chords with a nostalgic, psychedelic haze
chips.desc: Each Mellotron key plays an eight-second tape of a real flute, string or choir note. Its warbly flute opened 60s psychedelic and baroque pop records and is beloved by lo-fi producers.

chips.label: Melodica
chips.prompt: breathy melodica: reedy, harmonica-like keyboard melody blown through a mouthpiece, wistful and bright
chips.desc: A small keyboard you blow into, with free reeds like a harmonica; Hohner popularised it in the late 1950s. A dub reggae classic, also loved in indie and folk.

chips.label: Clean electric
chips.prompt: clean electric guitar: bright, glassy single-coil tone with light reverb, playing articulate chords and arpeggios
chips.desc: A single-coil guitar into a clean amp gives sparkle and definition. The default for pop, R&B, indie and neo-soul rhythm parts.

chips.label: Jangly 12-string
chips.prompt: jangly electric 12-string guitar: shimmering, chiming chords with doubled octave strings ringing out
chips.desc: Paired octave strings make every chord ring and shimmer. The jangle of mid-60s folk rock and 80s college-radio jangle pop.

chips.label: Crunchy overdrive
chips.prompt: crunchy overdriven electric guitar: warm tube-amp breakup on bluesy power chords and riffs
chips.desc: A tube amp pushed just past clean breaks up into warm crunch that responds to picking strength. The core of blues rock, classic rock and indie.

chips.label: High-gain distortion
chips.prompt: high-gain distorted electric guitar: thick, saturated wall of power chords with long, heavy sustain
chips.desc: Stacked gain stages compress humbuckers into a dense wall of harmonics. The engine of hard rock, metal and pop punk.

chips.label: Fuzz guitar
chips.prompt: buzzing fuzz guitar: thick, woolly, square-wave saturation on gritty, raw vintage riffs
chips.desc: Fuzz pedals, sold from the early 60s, clip the signal into a near-square wave for a buzzy, woolly, sustaining tone. The sound of 60s garage, psych, stoner rock and doom.

chips.label: Jazz hollow-body
chips.prompt: mellow jazz hollow-body guitar: warm, round, dark tone with smooth chord melodies and gentle comping
chips.desc: Big archtop hollow-bodies with neck humbuckers and flatwound strings give a warm, woody, rolled-off tone. The classic voice of jazz guitar from swing to bebop and soul jazz.

chips.label: 80s chorus clean
chips.prompt: chorus-drenched 80s clean guitar: shimmering, watery arpeggios with lush stereo chorus and echo
chips.desc: Boss's CE-1 chorus (1976) and the pedals that followed made clean guitars swirl and widen. The glassy, watery sound of 80s new wave, post-punk and dream pop.

chips.label: Surf twang
chips.prompt: surf twang guitar: drippy spring-reverb tone with fast tremolo-picked melodies on the low strings
chips.desc: Bright single-coils plus an early-60s spring reverb unit give surf rock its wet twang. Also beloved in spaghetti-western scores and retro garage.

chips.label: Shoegaze wall
chips.prompt: shoegaze wall of fuzz: layered, heavily distorted, reverse-reverb guitars with whammy-bar bends, dreamy and immense
chips.desc: Stacked fuzz, reverse reverb and constant tremolo-arm bending melt guitars into a roaring haze. Late-80s UK bands invented it, named for staring at their pedals.

chips.label: Baritone guitar
chips.prompt: deep baritone guitar: twangy, low-tuned notes between guitar and bass, moody and cinematic
chips.desc: A longer-scale guitar tuned a fourth or fifth below standard, often B to B. Its dark twang suits spaghetti-western scores, modern country and heavy riffs.

chips.label: Palm-muted chugs
chips.prompt: palm-muted chugging guitars: tight, percussive low-string chugs locked to the kick drum
chips.desc: Resting the picking hand on the strings by the bridge damps them into a tight 'chug'. The rhythmic backbone of metal, hard rock and pop punk verses.

chips.label: Funk scratch
chips.prompt: funky scratch guitar: muted sixteenth-note chicken-scratch strums and tight chord stabs
chips.desc: Muting the strings with the fretting hand while strumming fast 16ths gives the percussive 'chicken scratch'. Essential in funk, disco and Afrobeat rhythm sections.

chips.label: Wah-wah
chips.prompt: wah-wah guitar: vocal, sweeping 'wacka-wacka' rhythm and crying lead lines through a foot pedal
chips.desc: A foot-controlled filter sweep, introduced in the late 60s, makes the guitar talk. Famous in 70s funk and soul soundtracks and psychedelic rock solos.

chips.label: Slide guitar
chips.prompt: bluesy slide guitar: a glass bottleneck gliding between notes, wailing and vocal, in open tuning
chips.desc: A glass or metal tube, originally a bottle neck, slides along the strings for crying glissandi. A Delta blues tradition that runs through Southern rock and Americana.

chips.label: E-bow swells
chips.prompt: ambient e-bow guitar swells: endlessly sustained, violin-like notes fading in and out with lush reverb
chips.desc: The EBow, a handheld magnetic device from the 1970s, keeps a string vibrating indefinitely so the guitar sustains like a bowed instrument. Used in post-rock, ambient and dream pop.

chips.label: Tremolo picking
chips.prompt: rapid tremolo-picked guitar: fast, continuous single-note picking in a shimmering, intense melodic wash
chips.desc: Picking one note as fast as possible makes it hover and shimmer. Core to surf, black metal and post-rock crescendos.

chips.label: Highlife guitar
chips.prompt: bright Afrobeat and highlife guitar: clean, interlocking looping single-note patterns and sparkling picked chords
chips.desc: Ghanaian highlife and Nigerian Afrobeat use clean, trebly guitars playing short repeating patterns that interlock like percussion. Their sunny, cyclical lines live on in modern Afrobeats and soukous.

chips.label: Reggae skank
chips.prompt: reggae skank guitar: short, choppy, trebly chord upstrokes on the offbeat, crisp and bouncing
chips.desc: Short chord chops on the offbeats, damped right after each strum, give ska, rocksteady and reggae their bounce. Often doubled by an organ 'bubble'.

chips.label: Rock guitar solo
chips.prompt: soaring rock guitar solo: singing sustain, wide string bends, vibrato and fast pentatonic runs
chips.desc: A lead guitar pushed into smooth sustain sings like a voice. Bends, vibrato and pentatonic runs are the language of classic rock, hard rock and power ballads.

chips.label: Blues licks
chips.prompt: stinging electric blues guitar: expressive bent notes and call-and-response licks between the vocal lines
chips.desc: Blues players bend notes between the minor and major third and answer the singer phrase by phrase. The root of rock, soul and R&B lead guitar.

chips.label: Twinkly tapping
chips.prompt: twinkly tapped clean guitar: intricate two-hand tapped arpeggios cascading in odd time signatures
chips.desc: Tapping with both hands on the fretboard creates rippling, piano-like arpeggios. The signature of math rock and Midwest emo's 'twinkly' sound.

chips.label: Nylon classical
chips.prompt: warm nylon-string classical guitar: soft, round fingerpicked melodies and gentle arpeggiated chords
chips.desc: Nylon strings sound softer and rounder than steel. Played fingerstyle, it is the guitar of classical, bossa nova and Latin ballads, and a lo-fi favourite.

chips.label: Fingerpicked acoustic
chips.prompt: fingerpicked steel-string acoustic guitar: bright, intimate arpeggios over alternating-thumb bass notes
chips.desc: The thumb alternates between bass strings while the fingers pick a melody, a style from early country and blues. The intimate engine of folk, country and singer-songwriter music.

chips.label: Strummed acoustic
chips.prompt: strummed steel-string acoustic guitar: bright, full open chords in a driving campfire rhythm
chips.desc: A big-bodied dreadnought acoustic strummed with a pick fills the mid-range with shimmer. The heartbeat of folk, country, pop and acoustic rock.

chips.label: Flamenco guitar
chips.prompt: fiery flamenco guitar: rapid rasgueado strums, percussive golpe taps and dramatic Phrygian runs
chips.desc: A light, bright nylon-string guitar fitted with a tap plate. Finger-flicked rasgueado strums and Phrygian-mode runs drive Andalusian flamenco and its rumba offshoots.

chips.label: Pedal steel
chips.prompt: weeping pedal steel guitar: smooth swelling bends and sliding chords, tearful and sweet
chips.desc: Played flat with a steel bar, plus pedals and knee levers that bend single strings inside a chord. The tearful cry of classic country, honky-tonk and Americana.

chips.label: Resonator guitar
chips.prompt: metallic resonator guitar: bright, ringing, nasal tone with slide licks for bluegrass and blues
chips.desc: Aluminium cones inside the body make it loud and tangy; the Dobro is the best-known brand. Played lap-style in bluegrass or with a bottleneck in Delta blues.

chips.label: Lush strings
chips.prompt: lush orchestral string section: sweeping legato violins, violas and cellos, warm and cinematic
chips.desc: A full section of 30 to 60 players bowing smooth legato lines in harmony. The emotional swell behind film scores, ballads, disco and Bollywood.

chips.label: Staccato strings
chips.prompt: driving staccato strings: short, punchy, rhythmic ostinato bowing pushing the music forward
chips.desc: Short, detached bow strokes repeated as a rhythmic ostinato. The pulse of action trailers, epic scores and orchestral pop builds.

chips.label: Pizzicato
chips.prompt: playful pizzicato strings: plucked violins and cellos, light, bouncy and mischievous
chips.desc: Strings plucked with the fingers instead of bowed. Bouncy and light: tiptoeing comedy, holiday music and quirky indie pop.

chips.label: Tremolo strings
chips.prompt: suspenseful tremolo strings: rapid shivering bow strokes, tense and shimmering
chips.desc: Moving the bow back and forth very fast makes notes shiver. Classic for suspense, horror and building tension, or a shimmering bed in ambient scores.

chips.label: Solo cello
chips.prompt: expressive solo cello: deep, warm, singing melody with rich vibrato and long bow strokes
chips.desc: The cello's range sits closest to the human voice, from deep bass to singing tenor. Mournful and intimate in neo-classical, film and sad piano pieces.

chips.label: Solo violin
chips.prompt: soaring solo violin: sweet, expressive melody with vibrato and graceful slides
chips.desc: The highest bowed string, agile and singing. Used for virtuosic leads in classical, crossover, film themes and emotional pop bridges.

chips.label: Solo viola
chips.prompt: warm solo viola: dark, husky mid-range melody with gentle vibrato
chips.desc: Slightly larger than a violin and tuned a fifth lower, the viola has a dark, husky warmth. Moody and introspective, a secret weapon of chamber pop.

chips.label: Double bass section
chips.prompt: deep double bass section: dark bowed low notes and heavy pizzicato under the orchestra
chips.desc: The orchestra's lowest strings, usually six to eight players. They give film scores ominous weight with long bowed tones and thumping pizzicato.

chips.label: Harp
chips.prompt: concert harp: shimmering glissandos and delicate plucked arpeggios, dreamy and celestial
chips.desc: The 47-string pedal harp can sweep a glissando across every string. Its rippling arpeggios signal dreams, flashbacks and magic in film, and warm up ballads and dream pop.

chips.label: Full orchestra
chips.prompt: full symphony orchestra in tutti: strings, brass, woodwinds and timpani swelling together in a grand climax
chips.desc: A symphony orchestra of 60 to 100 players, everyone playing at once (tutti). The biggest acoustic sound there is, built for film climaxes, anthems and epic trailers.

chips.label: String quartet
chips.prompt: intimate string quartet: two violins, viola and cello weaving close, expressive harmony
chips.desc: The chamber format perfected in the late 18th century. Detailed and intimate; great for indie ballads, baroque pop and string covers of pop songs.

chips.label: Brass section
chips.prompt: punchy horn section: tight trumpets, trombones and saxophones playing bright unison riffs and stabs
chips.desc: A horn section of trumpet, sax and trombone playing tight unison lines and stabs. It drives soul, funk, ska, big-band swing and pop.

chips.label: French horns
chips.prompt: noble French horns: warm, heroic, round brass melody soaring over the orchestra
chips.desc: Played with a hand in the bell, horns have a warm, round, heroic tone; film orchestras often use four to eight. The voice of adventure and nobility in film scores.

chips.label: Muted trumpet
chips.prompt: smoky muted trumpet: intimate, breathy, buzzy tone through a Harmon mute, late-night jazz
chips.desc: A Harmon mute in the bell gives a buzzy, whispering, intimate sound. Iconic in cool jazz ballads, noir soundtracks and jazzy lo-fi.

chips.label: Trumpet fanfare
chips.prompt: bright trumpet fanfare: bold, triumphant brass calls with crisp tonguing and ringing high notes
chips.desc: Short heraldic calls built on chord tones, born in ceremony and battle. Used for royal, sporting, victory and epic opening moments.

chips.label: Trombone
chips.prompt: warm trombone: rich, buttery brass lines with smooth slides and punchy accents
chips.desc: The slide lets trombones glide between notes. Warm and mellow in ballads, punchy in ska, salsa and big-band shout choruses.

chips.label: Tuba
chips.prompt: deep orchestral tuba: weighty, round low brass anchoring dramatic chords
chips.desc: The largest, lowest brass instrument. In the orchestra it anchors the brass with dark, massive weight in film and epic scores.

chips.label: Trailer braams
chips.prompt: massive trailer brass braams: huge, distorted low-brass blasts with booming impacts, dark and epic
chips.desc: Since around 2010, blockbuster trailers have used enormous low-brass 'braams', often layered with synths and hits. Shorthand for epic, ominous scale.

chips.label: Alto sax
chips.prompt: smooth alto saxophone: bright, singing, expressive melody with soulful bends
chips.desc: The alto is the agile, bright, singing member of the sax family. Heard in bebop, smooth jazz, R&B and 80s pop solos.

chips.label: Tenor sax
chips.prompt: warm, breathy tenor saxophone: husky, soulful lead with growls and smoky vibrato
chips.desc: Lower and huskier than the alto, the tenor is the classic sax voice of jazz ballads, honking rock and roll and R&B solos.

chips.label: Baritone sax
chips.prompt: growling baritone saxophone: deep, honking low riffs adding punch under the horn section
chips.desc: The big low sax grunts bass lines and punchy riffs beneath the horns. Essential in funk, soul, ska and swing.

chips.label: Clarinet
chips.prompt: woody clarinet: warm, smooth melody moving from dark low notes to bright high runs
chips.desc: A single-reed woodwind with a huge range: hollow and dark down low, sweet and bright up high. Key in classical, klezmer, Dixieland and early jazz.

chips.label: Flute
chips.prompt: airy concert flute: breathy, light, flowing melody floating above the arrangement
chips.desc: A transverse flute with a pure, breathy tone. It brings pastoral calm, birdsong and floating melody to classical, film, jazz and psychedelic rock.

chips.label: Piccolo
chips.prompt: piercing piccolo: tiny, bright, high-flying runs and trills cutting through the full orchestra
chips.desc: Half the size of a flute and an octave higher, it pierces through everything. Used in marches and festive or comic passages.

chips.label: Oboe
chips.prompt: plaintive oboe: nasal, reedy, poignant melody, pastoral and lyrical
chips.desc: A double-reed woodwind with a penetrating, bittersweet voice. The orchestra tunes to its A, and it carries pastoral, lonely and tender themes.

chips.label: Bassoon
chips.prompt: dry, woody bassoon: reedy low notes bouncing in playful or wistful lines
chips.desc: The bass of the double-reed family. Its dry, woody tone can be comic and grumpy or soulful and melancholy.

chips.label: SATB choir
chips.prompt: full SATB choir: soprano, alto, tenor and bass voices singing wordless 'aah' harmonies, rich and cathedral-like
chips.desc: SATB stands for soprano, alto, tenor and bass, the four sections of a standard mixed choir. Wordless choir pads add grandeur to film scores, epic trailers and ballads.

chips.label: Boys' choir
chips.prompt: angelic boys' choir: pure, high, bright treble voices echoing through a stone church
chips.desc: Unbroken treble voices with a pure, bright, nearly vibrato-free tone. The sound of the English cathedral tradition and ethereal, sacred moments in film.

chips.label: Gospel choir
chips.prompt: powerful gospel choir: soulful call-and-response harmonies, handclaps and soaring belted chords
chips.desc: Born in African-American churches, gospel choirs sing stacked, bluesy harmonies with call-and-response and huge dynamic builds. They lift soul, R&B, house and pop choruses.

chips.label: Chanting choir
chips.prompt: chanting choir: deep, unison male voices intoning slow, ancient monastic chant in a vast stone reverb
chips.desc: Gregorian and Orthodox chant are unaccompanied vocal lines, often over a held drone. Deep chanting voices add mystery, ritual and epic darkness to scores and games.

chips.label: Timpani
chips.prompt: rolling orchestral timpani: deep, tuned kettle-drum rolls and booming dramatic hits
chips.desc: Copper kettle drums tuned to exact notes with foot pedals. Their rolls and thunderous accents add drama to classical climaxes, film scores and trailers.

chips.label: Glockenspiel
chips.prompt: sparkling glockenspiel: bright, ringing metal-bar melody, twinkling and festive
chips.desc: Steel bars struck with hard mallets give a bright, ringing chime. It twinkles on top of film scores, Christmas music, 60s pop and indie.

chips.label: Marimba
chips.prompt: warm wooden marimba: round, mellow mallet tones in rolling, rhythmic patterns
chips.desc: Rosewood bars over tuned tube resonators, with roots in African and Central American instruments. Warm and percussive in minimalism, Latin music, tropical house and pop.

chips.label: Vibraphone
chips.prompt: cool vibraphone: shimmering, vibrato-laced metal bars struck with soft mallets, mellow and jazzy
chips.desc: Aluminium bars with motor-driven discs spinning in the resonators create a pulsing vibrato. A cool jazz, lounge and lo-fi favourite since the 1930s.

chips.label: Xylophone
chips.prompt: bright, dry xylophone: crisp, woody, staccato mallet notes, playful and bouncy
chips.desc: Hard rosewood or synthetic bars give a dry, bright, short tone. Used for skeletal, comic or playful effects in cartoons and orchestral scores.

chips.label: Tubular bells
chips.prompt: resonant tubular bells: deep, chiming church-bell tones ringing out in slow, solemn strikes
chips.desc: Long brass tubes struck with a mallet stand in for church bells in the orchestra. Ominous, ceremonial or celebratory; a horror and sacred-music staple.

chips.label: Sitar
chips.prompt: shimmering sitar: buzzing, twangy plucked melody with sweeping bends and ringing sympathetic strings over a drone
chips.desc: The long-necked lute of Hindustani classical music, with a curved bridge that makes notes buzz and up to 13 sympathetic strings that ring along. It swept into 60s psychedelic rock and pop.

chips.label: Tabla
chips.prompt: intricate tabla: crisp, ringing high drum and deep, bending bass drum in fast, rolling rhythmic patterns
chips.desc: A pair of hand drums: the small wooden dayan rings at a tuned pitch while the larger metal bayan's bass bends under the palm. The rhythmic heart of Hindustani music and Bollywood.

chips.label: Bansuri
chips.prompt: breathy bansuri bamboo flute: soft, airy, ornamented melody gliding between notes, meditative and pastoral
chips.desc: A side-blown bamboo flute of North India, long associated with the god Krishna. Its breathy, bending melodies suit Hindustani classical, devotional and film music.

chips.label: Shehnai
chips.prompt: festive shehnai: piercing, reedy double-reed melody with fast ornaments, bright and celebratory
chips.desc: A North Indian double-reed horn with a nasal, penetrating voice. Traditionally played at weddings, temples and festivals, it signals celebration and auspicious beginnings.

chips.label: Santoor
chips.prompt: sparkling santoor: rippling hammered-dulcimer notes, bright and cascading over a gentle drone
chips.desc: A Kashmiri hammered dulcimer with around 100 strings, struck with light curved mallets. Its shimmering cascades suit Hindustani classical, meditation and film music.

chips.label: Koto
chips.prompt: elegant Japanese koto: plucked zither notes with pitch bends and graceful, ringing pentatonic phrases
chips.desc: Japan's 13-string zither with movable bridges, plucked with finger picks. Pressing strings behind the bridges bends notes for its poised, elegant sound.

chips.label: Shamisen
chips.prompt: twangy shamisen: three-string Japanese lute struck with a big plectrum, percussive, snappy and fast
chips.desc: A skin-covered three-string lute struck with a large plectrum, so every note snaps. Its fast, virtuosic Tsugaru style has inspired rock and anime soundtracks.

chips.label: Shakuhachi
chips.prompt: breathy shakuhachi bamboo flute: airy, haunting, wavering tones with expressive breath accents
chips.desc: An end-blown Japanese bamboo flute once played as meditation by Zen monks. Its breathy, wavering tone evokes stillness, mist and mountains.

chips.label: Erhu
chips.prompt: expressive erhu: two-string Chinese fiddle with a soaring, voice-like, slightly nasal bowed melody and slides
chips.desc: A Chinese two-string fiddle with the bow hair threaded between the strings and a snakeskin-covered body. Its plaintive, voice-like slides carry Chinese folk, opera and film melodies.

chips.label: Guzheng
chips.prompt: flowing guzheng: rippling plucked zither glissandos and bent pentatonic notes, graceful and shimmering
chips.desc: A Chinese zither, usually with 21 strings over movable bridges, tuned to a pentatonic scale. Sweeping glissandos and left-hand bends give it a flowing, water-like sound.

chips.label: Pipa
chips.prompt: agile pipa: bright, percussive four-string Chinese lute with rapid tremolo and dramatic strums
chips.desc: A pear-shaped four-string Chinese lute with over 2,000 years of history. Its rapid five-finger tremolo and martial strums can sound delicate or battle-ready.

chips.label: Gamelan
chips.prompt: shimmering Indonesian gamelan: interlocking bronze metallophones, deep gongs and drums in cycling, hypnotic patterns
chips.desc: The bronze ensembles of Java and Bali: metallophones, gong chimes, great gongs and kendang drums. Interlocking parts in their own slendro and pelog scales shimmer and cycle around the big gong.

chips.label: Oud
chips.prompt: warm oud: fretless short-neck lute with deep, woody plucked notes, sliding ornaments and maqam melodies
chips.desc: The fretless short-necked lute of the Arab world, Turkey and Iran, and ancestor of the European lute. Its smooth fingerboard lets players slide through the microtones of maqam scales.

chips.label: Qanun
chips.prompt: glittering qanun: rapid plucked zither runs and shimmering tremolos, ornate and bright
chips.desc: A trapezoid zither with about 78 strings in courses of three, plucked with finger picks. Small levers re-tune strings mid-song for microtonal maqam scales.

chips.label: Darbuka
chips.prompt: crisp darbuka goblet drum: deep 'doum' bass and sharp 'tek' rim hits in rapid, rolling Middle Eastern rhythms
chips.desc: A goblet drum played across North Africa, the Middle East and Turkey. Its deep doum and crisp tek strokes drive belly dance, Arabic pop and Turkish music.

chips.label: Bouzouki
chips.prompt: bright Greek bouzouki: metallic, tremolo-picked long-neck lute melodies, lively and dancing
chips.desc: A long-necked Greek lute with paired metal strings, the voice of rebetiko and Greek popular music. An adapted version became a staple of Irish folk from the 1960s.

chips.label: Ney flute
chips.prompt: breathy ney flute: haunting, airy end-blown reed flute melody with slow, mystical ornaments
chips.desc: An end-blown reed flute of Persian, Arabic and Turkish music, central to Sufi ceremonies. Its breathy, sighing tone sounds spiritual and ancient.

chips.label: Duduk
chips.prompt: mournful duduk: dark, warm, sorrowful double-reed melody over a sustained drone
chips.desc: An Armenian double-reed flute carved from apricot wood, usually played over a second duduk holding a drone. Its sorrowful warmth is much loved in film scores.

chips.label: Bağlama saz
chips.prompt: twangy Turkish bağlama saz: bright, metallic long-neck lute melodies with fast, ringing strummed patterns
chips.desc: The long-necked lute at the heart of Turkish, Kurdish and Anatolian folk music. Bright metal strings and microtonal frets give it a ringing, nasal twang.

chips.label: Kalimba
chips.prompt: gentle kalimba thumb piano: soft, plinking metal tines in a sweet, looping melody with a warm, woody body
chips.desc: A modern box-bodied thumb piano based on the mbira family of Africa. Its plinky, music-box-like tone is a favourite in lo-fi, Afro-pop and gentle children's music.

chips.label: Mbira
chips.prompt: buzzing Zimbabwean mbira: interlocking metal-key patterns with a bright rattling buzz inside a resonant gourd
chips.desc: The Shona people's mbira has 22 to 28 metal keys and bottle-cap buzzers, often played inside a gourd. Its interlocking cyclical patterns accompany ceremonies that call on ancestors.

chips.label: Kora
chips.prompt: flowing kora: rippling 21-string West African harp-lute with cascading, interlocking arpeggios and bright bass runs
chips.desc: The 21-string harp-lute of the Mande griots of Mali, Senegal, Gambia and Guinea. Its flowing, harp-like runs carry centuries of praise songs and modern Afro-pop.

chips.label: Balafon
chips.prompt: bright balafon: wooden West African xylophone with buzzing gourd resonators in fast, cyclical melodies
chips.desc: A wooden xylophone of the Mande world, with gourd resonators fitted with buzzing membranes. Its rattling, woody patterns drive West African griot and dance music.

chips.label: Talking drum
chips.prompt: pitch-bending talking drum: hourglass drum squeezed under the arm, swooping and speaking in rhythmic phrases
chips.desc: An hourglass drum (the Yoruba dundun) whose pitch rises when the player squeezes its cords. It mimics the tones of speech and drives juju, fuji and Afrobeats.

chips.label: Amapiano log drum
chips.prompt: deep amapiano log drum: woody, pitched, bouncing bass-percussion hits sliding through syncopated patterns
chips.desc: Amapiano's signature, born in South Africa's townships in the mid-2010s: a deep, woody synth hit that plays the bassline like a drum. Pairs with shakers and jazzy keys around 112 BPM.

chips.label: Steel pan
chips.prompt: bright Caribbean steel pan: sweet, ringing metallic melody with rolled notes, sunny and tropical
chips.desc: Invented in Trinidad and Tobago in the 1930s and 40s from oil drums hammered into tuned note areas. Its sweet, ringing voice is the sound of calypso, soca and carnival.

chips.label: Charango
chips.prompt: sparkling Andean charango: small ten-string lute strummed in bright, fast, ringing rhythms
chips.desc: A small Andean lute with five pairs of strings, traditionally built with an armadillo-shell back. Its bright, jangly strums lead Bolivian and Peruvian folk.

chips.label: Pan flute
chips.prompt: airy Andean pan flute: breathy, hollow panpipe melody with soft, fluttering accents
chips.desc: Rows of bamboo pipes of different lengths, like the Andean siku and zampona, blown across the top. Breathy and evocative of mountains, Andean folk and new age.

chips.label: Cuatro
chips.prompt: bright cuatro: small Latin American folk guitar strumming crisp, fast, syncopated rhythms
chips.desc: Two Latin guitars share the name: Venezuela's four-string cuatro strums the rhythm of joropo, while Puerto Rico's ten-string cuatro sings bright melodies in jibaro music.

chips.label: Bandoneon
chips.prompt: dramatic bandoneon: breathy, melancholic button-accordion chords and sharp staccato tango phrases
chips.desc: A German square concertina that became the soul of Argentine tango in the early 20th century. Its bellows sigh and snap with passion and melancholy.

chips.label: Berimbau
chips.prompt: twangy berimbau: single-string musical bow with a gourd, buzzing and wah-like, tapped in a hypnotic rhythm
chips.desc: A Brazilian musical bow: a steel string struck with a stick while a gourd pressed to the belly opens and closes for a 'wah'. It leads the music of capoeira.

chips.label: Cuban tres
chips.prompt: bright Cuban tres: three doubled-string guitar playing crisp, syncopated montuno riffs
chips.desc: A Cuban guitar with three pairs of strings, tuned so its sharp, ringing montuno riffs cut through. The lead guitar voice of son cubano and an ancestor of salsa.

chips.label: Bagpipes
chips.prompt: stirring Highland bagpipes: loud, droning reedy pipes with a soaring chanter melody and ornamented grace notes
chips.desc: The Great Highland bagpipe sounds three drones under a nine-note chanter, fed by a bag of air. Martial, mournful and stirring at Scottish ceremonies.

chips.label: Tin whistle
chips.prompt: lilting tin whistle: bright, breathy six-hole flute playing ornamented Irish jig and reel melodies
chips.desc: A cheap six-hole whistle at the centre of Irish traditional music. Cuts and rolls give it a lilting, dancing sparkle.

chips.label: Uilleann pipes
chips.prompt: sweet uilleann pipes: soft, plaintive Irish bagpipes with a reedy two-octave melody over warm drones
chips.desc: Irish bagpipes filled by an elbow bellows instead of the breath, sweeter and quieter than Highland pipes. Keyed regulators add chords for mournful airs and fast reels alike.

chips.label: Bodhrán
chips.prompt: driving bodhrán: Irish frame drum beaten with a double-ended stick, pitch-shaped by the hand inside
chips.desc: An Irish frame drum played with a small double-ended stick while the other hand presses the skin from inside to change pitch. The rhythmic pulse of Irish jigs and reels.

chips.label: Accordion
chips.prompt: lively accordion: bellows-driven reedy chords and bouncy melody, warm and folky
chips.desc: A free-reed instrument driven by bellows, with keys or buttons for melody and chords. Heard in French musette, polka, Irish trad, Cajun, zydeco, Mexican norteno and Colombian vallenato.

chips.label: Hurdy-gurdy
chips.prompt: droning hurdy-gurdy: cranked-wheel strings buzzing over a constant drone with a rasping medieval melody
chips.desc: A medieval string instrument: a rosined wheel turned by a crank bows the strings while keys press the melody. Its buzzing drones suit folk, neofolk and folk metal.

chips.label: Balalaika
chips.prompt: fast tremolo balalaika: bright, triangular three-string Russian lute strummed in lively folk-dance patterns
chips.desc: A Russian lute with a triangular body and three strings. Rapid tremolo strumming gives Russian folk its bright, galloping energy.

chips.label: Hang drum
chips.prompt: meditative hang drum: soft, ringing, steel-pan-like tones tapped by hand, warm and hypnotic
chips.desc: The Hang was created in Bern, Switzerland, in 2000; similar instruments are called handpans. Two steel shells tuned to a scale ring with a calm, otherworldly glow.

chips.label: Banjo
chips.prompt: bright, rolling five-string banjo: fast three-finger picking patterns, twangy and driving
chips.desc: Descended from West African gourd lutes brought to the Americas by enslaved people. Bluegrass three-finger rolls and old-time clawhammer make it the twang of Appalachian music.

chips.label: Mandolin
chips.prompt: crisp mandolin: bright paired strings with tremolo melodies and choppy bluegrass backbeat chords
chips.desc: An Italian lute with four pairs of strings tuned like a violin. Its sharp 'chop' backbeat and tremolo melodies drive bluegrass, Italian folk and folk rock.

chips.label: Fiddle
chips.prompt: lively fiddle: violin played folk-style with driving bow rhythms, slides and double stops
chips.desc: The same instrument as the violin, played in dance-music styles. Celtic reels, bluegrass breakdowns, Cajun waltzes and country all live on fiddle.

chips.label: Harmonica
chips.prompt: wailing blues harmonica: bent, breathy reedy notes and chugging train rhythms
chips.desc: A pocket free-reed instrument. Blues players use 'cross harp' and bend notes with the mouth for its crying wail; also a folk and country staple.

chips.label: Appalachian dulcimer
chips.prompt: sweet Appalachian dulcimer: plucked lap zither melody over ringing drone strings, gentle and old-time
chips.desc: A fretted zither laid across the lap, playing melody over drone strings. A folk-revival favourite with roots in Appalachian mountain music.

chips.label: Ukulele
chips.prompt: cheerful ukulele: bright, plinky nylon-string strums and sweet, sunny chords
chips.desc: A four-string Hawaiian guitar developed from Portuguese instruments brought to Hawaii in 1879. Its bright, happy strum suits island music, indie pop and feel-good ads.

chips.label: Didgeridoo
chips.prompt: deep didgeridoo: earthy, buzzing drone with rhythmic vocal pulses, circular-breathed and hypnotic
chips.desc: An Aboriginal Australian wind instrument from northern Australia, made from eucalyptus hollowed by termites. Circular breathing keeps its deep, buzzing drone going.

chips.label: Standard E
chips.prompt: guitars in standard E tuning: bright, familiar open-chord voicings and balanced, ringing strings
chips.desc: E A D G B E, low to high. The default tuning almost every chord chart assumes; bright and balanced for pop, folk, blues and rock.

chips.label: Drop D
chips.prompt: guitars in drop D with heavy, resonant low-string riffs and one-finger power chords
chips.desc: D A D G B E: only the low E drops a whole step. Easy one-finger power chords and a deeper low end; loved by grunge, alt-rock and metal players and folk fingerpickers.

chips.label: Drop C
chips.prompt: guitars in drop C: crushing, down-tuned chugging riffs with a thick, dark low end
chips.desc: C G C F A D: everything down a whole step, then the lowest string down another. The heavy, saturated chug of metalcore, nu-metal and post-hardcore.

chips.label: D standard
chips.prompt: guitars tuned a whole step down to D standard: darker, looser, heavier chords and easy bends
chips.desc: D G C F A D, every string down a whole step. Slacker strings bend easily and sound darker; heard in grunge, doom, stoner rock and heavy blues.

chips.label: Eb (half-step down)
chips.prompt: guitars tuned a half step down to E-flat: warm, slightly darker tone, slinky bends and fat chords
chips.desc: Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb. A half step down loosens the strings for easier bends and suits lower voices; common in 80s hard rock, blues rock and shred.

chips.label: DADGAD
chips.prompt: guitar in DADGAD tuning: droning, open, modal chords ringing with a Celtic, harp-like shimmer
chips.desc: D A D G A D, an open suspended tuning with no third, so chords sound ambiguous and droning. Popularised in 1960s British folk; a Celtic and fingerstyle favourite.

chips.label: Open G
chips.prompt: guitar in open G tuning: ringing, bluesy open chords and slide riffs with a raw, droning edge
chips.desc: D G D G B D, so the open strings strum a G chord. Delta slide players and rock rhythm guitarists use it for big droning riffs, sometimes removing the low string.

chips.label: Open D
chips.prompt: guitar in open D tuning: big, resonant open chords and slide lines over a full, droning low end
chips.desc: D A D F# A D, a full D major chord on the open strings. Deep and resonant for slide blues, folk and fingerstyle ballads.

chips.label: Open E
chips.prompt: guitar in open E tuning: bright, high-tension open chords and wailing electric slide
chips.desc: E B E G# B E, an open E major chord at higher string tension than open D. Bright and punchy for electric slide blues and Southern rock.

chips.label: Nashville tuning
chips.prompt: shimmering Nashville-tuned acoustic guitar: high, chiming chords like a delicate 12-string
chips.desc: The four lowest strings are swapped for thin ones tuned an octave higher, borrowed from a 12-string set. Studio players double strummed parts with it for sparkle in country and pop.

chips.label: Baritone B
chips.prompt: baritone guitar tuned B to B: deep, dark, twangy low riffs and cinematic chords
chips.desc: B E A D F# B, a perfect fourth below standard on a longer-scale guitar. Dark and twangy for surf, western scores, modern country and metal.

chips.label: 7-string low B
chips.prompt: seven-string guitars with a low B: extended-range djent-style chugs and deep, wide chords
chips.desc: B E A D G B E: standard tuning plus a low B string. Mass-produced from 1990, it drove nu-metal and is now standard in progressive metal and djent.

chips.label: A=440 Hz
chips.prompt: instruments tuned to standard A=440 Hz concert pitch: bright, precise, modern tuning
chips.desc: The international reference since a 1939 conference: the A above middle C vibrates 440 times per second. Modern instruments, synths and recordings use it by default.

chips.label: A=432 Hz
chips.prompt: instruments tuned to A=432 Hz: slightly lower, warm, mellow pitch with a soft, dark resonance
chips.desc: About 32 cents (a third of a semitone) below 440. Fans call it warmer and calmer; science has found nothing special about it, but it is popular in meditation and ambient music.

chips.label: A=415 baroque
chips.prompt: period instruments at baroque pitch A=415 Hz: dark, gentle, gut-string warmth
chips.desc: Historically informed baroque ensembles tune about a semitone below modern pitch, to A=415. Gut strings and lower tension give a darker, gentler tone.
